# portable_goldens

> A Flutter golden-file comparator that makes exact golden tests pass on every machine. Each
> golden is compared, pixel for pixel, against THIS machine's render of the commit that last
> changed the golden, built once in a throwaway git worktree and cached per machine. The
> committed pngs stay as they are, for review and for runs without git history. There is no
> tolerance.

Read README.md for the full design. This file is the short version for an agent that is adding
the package to a project, running its goldens, or changing this package.

## When it is the right tool

- Goldens committed on one machine fail on another with a handful of pixels at anti-aliased
  edges, on the same Flutter version. (Measured cause: a macOS version difference alone.)
- The project wants exact compares, not a tolerance, and one set of committed pngs.

It is NOT the right tool when:

- the repository has no git history available (a shallow CI clone falls back to plain compares);
- the tests use a package that installs its own comparator inside each test, such as alchemist's
  `goldenTest`; it replaces this comparator for the test;
- the tests run on Windows (not supported yet: written for, never run there).

## Adding it to a project

1. `dev_dependencies: portable_goldens: ^0.1.0`
2. Create `test/flutter_test_config.dart`:

   ```dart
   import 'dart:async';

   import 'package:portable_goldens/portable_goldens.dart';

   Future<void> testExecutable(FutureOr<void> Function() testMain) async {
     PortableGoldenComparator.install();
     await testMain();
   }
   ```

   If the file already exists, add the `install()` call before `await testMain()`. If another
   comparator is already set there, `install()` leaves it and says so once on stderr;
   `install(strict: true)` throws instead.
3. Leave the tests alone: they keep calling `matchesGoldenFile`.
4. In CI, check out with full history (`fetch-depth: 0` on GitHub Actions) and cache
   `~/.cache/portable_goldens` (Linux) between runs. README.md, "In CI", has a workflow.

## Running goldens

Run these from the package root:

```sh
dart run portable_goldens:prepare   # build missing baselines now; exit 1 if a build failed
flutter test                       # compare
dart run portable_goldens:report    # failed goldens and goldens this branch changed; exit 1 on failure
dart run portable_goldens:verify    # before pushing: each committed png is what its commit draws here; exit 1 if not
dart run portable_goldens:prune     # remove baselines unused for 30 days, or of commits amended away here; --dry-run
```

`verify` is only meaningful on the machine that rendered the pngs: anywhere else every png
differs from its commit's render by the machine as well. A MISMATCH there means the png was
committed before its code, or with part of it (`git add -p`, a split rebase). It keeps the
committed png, the render and the diff in `.dart_tool/portable_goldens/verify/mismatches/`.

To change a golden on purpose: `flutter test --update-goldens`, look at the png, commit it. An
uncommitted png compares against itself in the working tree, so the run passes before the commit
too. Never "fix" a failure by re-rendering without looking at the diff in `failures/`.

## Reading a failure

Every failure message ends with `Compared exactly against <what>`:

| `<what>` | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `this machine's baseline, rendered from commit <sha>` | Current code draws differently from the commit that last changed the png, on this machine. A real regression, or an intended change. | Look at the diff images in `failures/`. If the change is intended, update and commit the golden. If the png was committed from this machine, run `verify`: the commit may not draw its own png. |
| `the png in the working tree, which differs from HEAD` | The uncommitted png does not match what the code draws now. | Re-render, or revert the png. |
| `the committed image, because <reason>` | Machine baselines were not used (see the reasons below), so this is a plain cross-machine compare and may be machine noise. | Fix the reason if you can (unshallow the clone, say). |

`Golden "<file>": <what> is unknown here, because it is a Git LFS pointer` means the png is in
Git LFS and its object is not here: run `git lfs install` and `git lfs pull`. Nothing was compared.

`portable_goldens could not build the baselines of commit <sha>` means the old commit's
submodules, `flutter pub get` or golden tests failed with today's SDK. The message carries the command, ready
to paste into a shell, and the end of its output. The usual fix: re-render that golden on the
current branch and commit it, which moves its baseline to a commit that builds.

Fallback reasons, printed once per test process. For the whole process (`SessionFallback`): no git
repository around the package; a shallow clone; a repository with no commit; no Flutter SDK; its
engine or framework revision cannot be found; the run is itself a baseline build (the one reason
never printed). For one golden (`GoldenFallback`, `CheckoutFailed`): the png is outside the
repository or the package; no commit has it; its commit cannot be checked out.
`CommittedBaseline.reason` is a sealed `FallbackReason`, so code can switch on it.

## Facts that are easy to get wrong

- The baseline is keyed by the commit that last changed the PNG (`git log -1 -- <png>`), not by
  HEAD, and is rendered by that commit's own tests.
- `--update-goldens` writes the committed png only. It never writes the machine cache.
- After an OS, engine, framework or Dart update, the machine key changes and every baseline is
  rebuilt, so an SDK upgrade does not fail goldens, as long as each commit still builds and
  passes on the new SDK. A pixel change from the SDK itself is not reported as a failure: the
  baseline and the test render with the same SDK.
- Rebase, amend and squash give commits new shas: their goldens' baselines are rebuilt, never
  wrong. What git cannot fix for you: a png committed ahead of or apart from its code (`verify`
  catches it), and inputs the commit does not track (untracked assets, ignored generated code),
  which the build's checkout lacks.
- The tests never check that a committed png matches its own commit's code, so a stale png
  passes them. Only `verify` checks it, on the machine that rendered the png.
- The cache lives outside the repository (macOS `~/Library/Caches/portable_goldens`, Linux
  `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/portable_goldens` or `~/.cache/portable_goldens`) and is shared by every
  worktree and clone. Override it with `PORTABLE_GOLDENS_CACHE`.
- The cache is shared by every repository, so `prune` removes a commit's baselines for being
  unreachable only when the repository it runs in has the commit; any other commit goes by age
  alone (`--older-than`, default 30 days). Removing a needed baseline costs a rebuild, never a
  wrong result.
- "Changed by this branch" is measured from the merge-base with the default branch. Override the
  ref with `PORTABLE_GOLDENS_BASE`.
- A build's checkout is not in your folder, so path dependencies outside the repository are
  given to it by a generated `pubspec_overrides.yaml`, from your own `.dart_tool/package_config.json`:
  they are the dependency as it is on disk now, not at the commit. Submodules are checked out with
  `git submodule update --init --recursive`, cloned from their URLs.
- Goldens in Git LFS are read through the commit's own filters, so they are the image wherever
  `git lfs` is installed. A pointer, where it is not, is never compared: it is reported as unknown.
- `PORTABLE_GOLDENS_CHILD=1` marks a baseline build. Never set it yourself.

## Working on this package

| Folder under `lib/src/` | Owns |
|---|---|
| `compare/` | `PortableGoldenComparator`: the compare, failure output, report entries |
| `session/` | `MachineGoldens` and the sealed `GoldensSession` (fallback or active): which baseline a golden uses, why it falls back (the sealed `FallbackReason`), branch changes |
| `machine/` | `MachineKey` (what goes in the key) and `FlutterSdk` (where the engine and framework revisions are read) |
| `store/` | `BaselineStore` and `CommitBaselines`: cache layout, lock, completion marker, build-mark-rename, sweep, atomic writes |
| `build/` | `BaselineBuilder`: the throwaway worktree and its submodules, `PathOverrides`, which test files to run, the child `flutter test`, which pngs it wrote |
| `git/` | `GitRepo` (every git question asked), `PackageLocation` (absolute, repo- and package-relative paths), `PathStyle` (every comparison of a path with a folder, `/` and `\`) and `CommitReachability` (is a commit still on a branch, tag or checkout) |
| `prune/` | `CacheInventory` (what the cache holds), `PrunePolicy` (what goes, and why) and `CachePruner` (removes it, under each unit's lock) |
| `process/` | `ProcessRunner`, the one seam every process launch goes through |
| `report/` | `GoldenReport` (the last run's outcomes) and `WorkSummary` (what `report` prints) |
| `verify/` | `GoldenVerifier` (is each committed png its commit's render here?), the sealed `GoldenCheck` results, and `PixelComparer`, whose `FlutterPixelComparer` runs one generated `flutter test` for the pixel compare |
| `cli/` | `GoldensCommand`, one class per command, the argument parser and `runPortableGoldens`; each `bin/<command>.dart` only calls it |

Rules the code already follows. Keep them:

- An unknown never passes. A build that fails throws `BuildFailure` and fails the golden; it is
  never treated as a match. A missing engine or framework revision falls back rather than
  trusting a key that cannot see an update.
- Only images the build wrote count, judged by mtime. A png checked out from git is another
  machine's image and is never taken for a render.
- Cache writes are atomic (a temporary file or folder, then a rename), because every test file
  runs in its own process and they all open the store at once.
- No dependencies beyond `flutter` and `flutter_test`, which is why `cli/` parses its own
  arguments.
- No `!` in `lib/` or `bin/`: `tool/check_null_assertions.sh` fails on one.
- A command never calls `exit` or touches `stdout` itself; it writes to its `CommandContext` and
  returns an `ExitCode`, so the tests run it in process.

Verify from the repository root with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed .`,
`flutter analyze --fatal-infos`, `flutter test`, `tool/check_null_assertions.sh` and
`tool/check_ignored_sources.sh`. The tests build real git repositories in temporary folders and
run real `git`. `tool/consumer_workflow.sh` runs the README's commands in a new consumer
repository, and requires a changed widget to fail; `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` runs all of these
on Linux and macOS.
